# Command-line reference

<!-- Generated by `isoloom docs --cli` from the command line's definition: don't edit. -->

Describe an environment once (machines, networks, ports), and get each tool's own files to run it: Compose, Kubernetes, Vagrant, Terraform, Ansible.

Global options:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--profile <NAME>` | Use a profile: `profiles/<name>.yml` in the project, what differs for one customer or site (target, spec values, defaults). Also `ISOLOOM_PROFILE`. |

## `isoloom validate`

Check the spec for mistakes (and that every path it mentions exists).

```text
Usage: isoloom validate [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--skip-files` | Don't check that files mentioned by the spec exist. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom targets`

List the targets the spec can be generated for, why the others can't, and the tier of each one generated (how far it has been proven).

```text
Usage: isoloom targets [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--json` | JSON instead of text. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom resources`

Add up the machines, CPUs, memory and disk the spec needs.

```text
Usage: isoloom resources [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--json` | JSON instead of text. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom generate`

Write each target's files under .isoloom/ (all possible targets, or one with --target).

```text
Usage: isoloom generate [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--target <TARGET>` | Only this target (any that `isoloom targets` lists); a profile's pinned target when it has one. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom check`

Fail when the generated files under .isoloom/ don't match the spec (for CI).

```text
Usage: isoloom check [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--target <TARGET>` | Only this target (any that `isoloom targets` lists); a profile's pinned target when it has one. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Only the files that fail, so a CI log shows what to fix. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one result per file, then a summary. |

## `isoloom defaults`

The defaults in effect here (built in, your file, the project's, the environment) and where each comes from. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#defaults>.

```text
Usage: isoloom defaults [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--system` | Only the built-in layer. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output. |

## `isoloom graph`

Draw the environment: networks, machines with their addresses and ports, reach rules, gateways and the access machine. D2 by default; `--format dot` for Graphviz. With `-o x.svg` or `-o x.png` the diagram is rendered when `d2` (or `dot`) is installed.

```text
Usage: isoloom graph [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | `d2` (default) or `dot`. Default: `d2`. |
| `-o, --out <OUT>` | Write here instead of stdout; `.svg` and `.png` are rendered. |
| `--instance <N>` | Draw instance N (its blocks and name). |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom report`

Print a table about the environment: `addressing`, `ports`, `wiring` or `resources` (text, or `--md` for Markdown). `isoloom report list` names them.

```text
Usage: isoloom report [OPTIONS] <NAME> [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | The report. |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--md` | Markdown instead of aligned text. |
| `--instance <N>` | Report on instance N. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom message`

Print the spec's `message` (how to use the environment), its placeholders filled.

```text
Usage: isoloom message [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--instance <N>` | The message of instance N. |
| `--target <TARGET>` | The target it runs on, for the addresses machines have there (default: the spec's single target, else the spec's addresses). |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom inspect`

Show the resolved snapshot (what `.isoloom/resolved.json` holds): every address, routes, targets and checks, worked out from the spec. A dotted path narrows it: `isoloom inspect machines.web.addresses`, `isoloom inspect targets`.

```text
Usage: isoloom inspect [OPTIONS] [WHAT] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[WHAT]` | A dotted path into the snapshot (default: all of it). A folder here means the project. |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). |
| `--yaml` | YAML instead of JSON. |
| `--instance <N>` | The snapshot of instance N (1-99) of the spec: its own names, Docker blocks and published ports, as a runner makes them for several copies on one host. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom profiles`

List the project's profiles (`profiles/<name>.yml`) and check each against the spec: the names it uses, the spec it makes, and that its target can run it. Fails when one doesn't.

```text
Usage: isoloom profiles [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The project folder (holding isoloom.yml). Default: `.`. |
| `--json` | JSON instead of text. |
| `--images <FILE>` | Your own image table (YAML): OS images, and the access machine when the spec leaves it to the runner. See <https://www.isoloom.com/en/docs/configuration#the-image-table>. |
| `-s, --set <KEY=VALUE>` | Override a value for this command: `-s machines.web.os=ubuntu@24.04` on the spec, `-s defaults.cloud.aws.region=eu-west-1` on the defaults. Repeatable. |

## `isoloom schema`

Print the JSON Schema of isoloom.yml (for editors: completion, hover docs, errors).

```text
Usage: isoloom schema [OPTIONS]
```

## `isoloom import`

Draft an isoloom.yml from files you already have.

```text
Usage: isoloom import [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

## `isoloom import terraform`

From Terraform: the `.tf` files of a folder, read statically (variables, locals, `for_each` and count evaluated); VMs and subnets become the draft, the rest is listed.

```text
Usage: isoloom import terraform [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[DIR]` | The folder with the .tf files (default: the current folder). |
| `--out <OUT>` | Where to write isoloom.yml (default: next to the source). |
| `--force` | Replace an existing isoloom.yml. |
| `--stdout` | Print the draft instead of writing it. |

## `isoloom import vagrant`

From a Vagrantfile: Ruby runs it against a stand-in `Vagrant` module, so no VM is made, but the rest of its code runs on this computer as it would under Vagrant: import only a Vagrantfile you trust. The settings it makes become the draft; the rest is listed, with why.

```text
Usage: isoloom import vagrant [OPTIONS] [FILE]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[FILE]` | The Vagrantfile (default: ./Vagrantfile). |
| `--out <OUT>` | Where to write isoloom.yml (default: next to the source). |
| `--force` | Replace an existing isoloom.yml. |
| `--stdout` | Print the draft instead of writing it. |

## `isoloom import compose`

From a Compose file: what it says that the format can express goes into the draft; the rest is listed, with why.

```text
Usage: isoloom import compose [OPTIONS] [FILE]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[FILE]` | The Compose file (default: compose.yaml, compose.yml, docker-compose.yaml or docker-compose.yml in the current folder). |
| `--out <OUT>` | Where to write isoloom.yml (default: next to the source). |
| `--force` | Replace an existing isoloom.yml. |
| `--stdout` | Print the draft instead of writing it. |

## `isoloom docs`

Print a reference page generated from the code: `--spec` for docs/spec.md, `--matrix` for docs/matrix.md, `--cli` for docs/reference/cli.md.

```text
Usage: isoloom docs [OPTIONS] <--spec|--matrix|--cli>
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--spec` | The spec reference (docs/spec.md): every field, its type, default, allowed values and limits. |
| `--matrix` | The capability matrix (docs/matrix.md): what each target does with each spec field, and each target's tier with its evidence. |
| `--cli` | The command-line reference (docs/reference/cli.md): every command and its arguments. |

## `isoloom matrix`

Show what each target does with each spec field (✓ generated, ✗ refused, with the step that refuses and why, – not applicable), worked out from the generators themselves, and each target's tier with its evidence. `--json` for tools.

```text
Usage: isoloom matrix [OPTIONS]
```

Arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | The matrix as JSON: the columns with their tiers, every tier entry with its evidence, and each row's cell per column (its state, and for a refusal the step and reason). |
